text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- SERBIA --
POLITIKA

- Yugoslavia's isolation is not correct. Russia supports Yugoslavia's return to international organisations, including European political structures, said Igor Ivanov, deputy Russian foreign minister on arrival in Belgrade. Ivanov is expected to meet highest Yugoslav and Serbian authorities on Monday.
- Croatian Helsinki Board said attacks on refugees in Kostajnica were carried out according to well-known scenario.
- Refinery in Srpski Brod in Bosnia restarted its production after six years buying 20,000 tonnes of crude from Serbia's oil industry NIS Jugopetrol.
NASA BORBA
- Sales of 49 percent of Serbian telecommunications within country's postal and telecommunications company Holding PTT Srbija to Italian STET expected beginning of summer, company sources said.
- State owes health and social workers 500 million dinars and there are only five million dinars available in the fund, said Zvonimir Golubovic, secretary in Serbia's health ministry.
- Arms producers of Kragujevac will stop production and stage a street protest on Wednesday unless they are paid late wages, said Dragutin Stanojlovic of the arms factory trade union Nezavisnost.
- Montenegrin Democartic Party of Socialists of Cetinje proposes Milo Djukanovic, republic's prime minister, and Svetozar Marovic, republic's parliament speaker, as presidental candidates.
- Liberation Army of Kosovo calls for armed struggle.
- Serbian police arrests more than 30 Albanians in Kosovo for interogation after two policemen were wounded last Friday.
- Vesna Pesic, one of coalition Zajedno leaders says coalition must be preserved at any cost.
- Moscow has offered economic cooperation and Zurich promised assistance to Belgrade, said Belgrade mayor Zoran Djindjic after his visits to Russia and Switzerland.
- Yugoslav insurance companies to reform. New law to be implemented as of July. Cash funds to be guarantee for survival.
- Current consumption of petrol in Bosnian Serb Republic is only fifth of what it used to be before the war.
- A J.P Morgan expert says (on sales of Serbia's telecommunications) serious buyers cannot be attracted by private sale.
- Milan Djuric, president of the independent association of pensioners announced street protest at the end of May.
- Malcolm Rifkind, former British minister of foreign affairs, prevented investigation against Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic in The Hague war crimes tribunal.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- The European Union trade benefits will enable fruit and vegetables to be exported in the value of $164 million this year.
- Yugoslavia's integration in the world will reduce grey economy, said Milorad Miskovic, federal minister for internal trade.
- Yugoslav vine producers expect to export 30,000 tonnes of wine this year.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Zivko Sokolovacki, political coordiantor for Vojvodina of the Yugoslav United Left, said there was enough room in Serbia's constitution to further define Vojvodina as an autonomous province.
-- MONTENEGRO --
POBJEDA
- President of Montengrin Trade Unions Danilo Popovic participated in Trade Union congress of Italian Puglia region.
- Dekor, a wall paper factory from Rozaje, used only 10 percent of its capacities in 1996 and incured a three million dinars debt.

- Unpaid electricity bills to Elektrodistribucija power company from Herceg Novi amounted to 14 million dinars. Town's companies owing seven million dinars agreed to pay bills through different barter arrangements. The Yugoslav army owes 1.6 million dinars but has nothing to offer. -- Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254
